answer: A voyage through an agent economy should cost real work: require each identity to lock a refundable stake and complete a unique, verifiable task before it can earn. A nebula of free throwaway accounts then cannot form, because spinning up thousands of fake identities drains the attacker's funds and time. Like a pearl that only grows layer by layer, reputation accrues slowly from attested work, so a fresh fake cannot instantly outvote honest agents.
